source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Fans information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data readable/correct; every fan status fits actual status; fan speed correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes `/Chassis/FRU_SYS/Thermal`, indexes only 0..7 for a sixteen-channel `_R` family, and after piping `.Fans` attempts `.Fans[$i]` against the array. Name filtering alone cannot prove the intended rear-side or paired-rotor identities, units, limits or freshness.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly rejects eight-of-sixteen coverage and requires topology, unit-aware speed/status and a passive boundary, but leaves the bounded `_R` map and approved ranges as an engineering decision.

old_problem: The proposed selection cannot return authoritative 16-channel coverage and may return no intended objects because of its jq data-shape error. It also labels `_R` as rear without proving whether the platform means rear fan, rear rotor or another controller channel. The earlier review correctly demanded authority but kept the case Pending rather than parameterizing those Project facts.
disposition_reason: Treat `_R` as an exact Project-defined namespace, not a guessed meaning. Discover the real fan resources, enumerate the entire set, bind SPD_FAN1_R through SPD_FAN16_R independently to their approved physical/controller identities, compare fresh unit-aware speed and health against contextual limits, and reconcile actual WebUI detail. If `_R` denotes the paired rotor/side of the same fan assembly as `_F`, retain both identities and apply the approved pair relationship without allowing one side to substitute for the other.
decision_basis: XLSX row 971, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 972 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 972 / variant 656357a525234c9f.

DMTF supports modern Fan resources under a discovered ThermalSubsystem and legacy fan arrays under Thermal. Status, Location and speed data must be decoded according to the service-advertised schema rather than a fixed OEM URI.

The sixteen `_R` identities are a separate source case from the preceding sixteen `_F` identities. A paired physical assembly, shared controller or similar numeric reading does not permit deduplication or borrowed PASS evidence.
`_R` is vendor/project nomenclature. The authoritative topology may define rear side, rear rotor or another channel; the review must not freeze DeepSeek's unverified label into an OEM requirement.

ED-08, ED-14, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve WebUI evidence, approved limits, logs and independent variant coverage; ED-33 through ED-38 allow the topology/range package as runtime configuration while forbidding control, fan manipulation, stimulus, reset/power and retry.

test_case.test_name: Validate SPD_FAN1_R through SPD_FAN16_R and their approved physical or paired-rotor relationships independently
test_case.purpose: Verify every exact `_R` speed/status channel is present according to the Project population, maps unambiguously to the correct fan assembly/rotor/controller input, reports fresh acceptable state and unit-aware speed for the captured cooling context, and agrees with the actual BMC WebUI; retain any approved `_F`/`_R` pairing only as correlation, never as replacement coverage.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/chassis/firmware/WebUI identity and authoritative definition of `_R` for this platform
Complete SPD_FAN1_R..SPD_FAN16_R-to-physical fan/rotor/controller map, expected population and, where applicable, explicit `_F`/`_R` assembly pairing
Approved per-channel state/health, speed unit, acceptable range/threshold, pair-consistency tolerance and staleness policy by power/load/redundancy/control context
Service-root-discovered Chassis ThermalSubsystem/Fan collection or documented legacy Thermal fan representation with pagination and durable mapping
Schema-aware parsing of modern Fan SpeedPercent/SpeedRPM/Status/Location or legacy Reading/ReadingUnits/threshold properties
Actual rendered WebUI Fans table/detail mapping, trusted TLS/protected credentials, preserved SEL/audit acquisition, synchronized timestamps, redaction and evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and record current power, workload, cooling redundancy and fan-control context. Follow advertised Chassis thermal links to the modern Fan collection, or use the target's documented legacy Thermal representation; enumerate every page/member and preserve complete redacted raw responses. From the approved map, locate exactly SPD_FAN1_R..SPD_FAN16_R and bind each to its physical assembly/rotor/controller input without using array position or substring alone. Record identity/location, expected and observed presence, Status.State/Health, numeric reading, declared RPM/percent unit, applicable thresholds/ranges and timestamp/freshness. If the package defines `_F`/`_R` pairs, correlate their assembly identity and approved pair tolerance while retaining two separate verdict rows. Capture the actual rendered WebUI table and required details and reconcile all sixteen `_R` rows within approved sampling skew. Preserve baseline and post SEL/audit logs without clearing. Do not change fan override/PWM/thresholds, stop/disconnect/reseat a fan, inject faults, create workload, reset/reboot or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: The matrix contains exactly sixteen distinct `_R` rows with no missing, duplicate or ambiguous physical/controller mapping. Every expected channel has the correct presence, state and health and a fresh numeric reading in the approved unit and contextual range. Any declared `_F`/`_R` pair maps to the same approved assembly and satisfies its approved relationship while both variants remain independently evidenced. API/telemetry and actual WebUI agree, logs show no unexpected cooling event, and no control or system state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires 16-of-16 exact `_R` identity coverage, Project-authoritative suffix/topology, complete resource traversal, fresh unit-aware contextual range comparison, acceptable presence/state/health and actual WebUI evidence. Where a pair relationship is specified, both sides and the approved relationship must pass separately. An eight-index query, `_R` substring, collection order, aggregate health or evidence borrowed from `_F` cannot pass. Missing/extra/duplicate mapping, wrong pair/location/unit, stale/unparseable/out-of-range speed, unacceptable health, unexpected log or UI/API/reference disagreement is FAIL. Missing suffix definition, topology, context or approved thresholds is NOT READY, not an unresolved design decision.
safety_gate: Use certificate-verified protected read operations and advertised resource links/schema; never assume `FRU_SYS` or a universal `_R` meaning.
Keep all sixteen `_R` identities and this source variant independent from `_F`; only an approved topology may establish a paired relationship.
Distinguish actual tachometer RPM, normalized percent, requested control and override state; compare only compatible quantities in the recorded context.
Retain pre/post SEL and audit evidence; do not execute the source's generic log-clear preamble for this passive test.
Prohibit fan override/PWM/threshold writes, stop/disconnect/reseat, fault injection, workload stimulus, BMC/system reset or reboot and power transitions.
On a missing pair/channel, stale reading or cooling fault, stop and preserve evidence; never auto-retry by changing cooling or power state.
expected_evidence: Immutable target and schema identity, authoritative `_R` definition, sixteen-channel physical/controller map and optional `_F`/`_R` pairing table
Complete advertised modern Fan or legacy Thermal artifacts with member/page coverage, timestamps and hashes
Sixteen-row `_R` result matrix with location, population, state/health, speed/unit, contextual range/threshold, freshness and independent verdict
Optional pair-correlation results that retain both `_F` and `_R` source identities and show approved relationship/tolerance
Actual rendered WebUI fan table/detail visual artifacts with per-channel API/UI/reference reconciliation
Preserved pre/post logs, unchanged-control/no-stimulus proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. Stop on ambiguous `_R` semantics, missing/duplicate mapping, bad pair relation, stale/out-of-range telemetry or cooling fault; preserve and redact raw/UI/log evidence and obtain the authoritative mapping or limit. Do not clear logs, manipulate fans or controls, inject faults, add workload, reset/reboot, power-cycle or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: Source title, WebUI procedure and Criteria consistently demand sixteen `_R` channels. DeepSeek's eight-entry query and unsupported `rear` gloss are review defects, not a conflicting authoritative requirement.

blocked.reason: The passive sixteen-channel objective is well defined. The Project-specific suffix, topology/pairing and contextual speed policies are bounded configuration inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Authoritative `_R` meaning; sixteen-channel physical/controller map and population; optional `_F`/`_R` pairing; advertised resource shape; contextual unit/range/threshold/pair/freshness rules; WebUI mapping; trust and evidence policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY `_R` FAN TELEMETRY REVIEW ONLY; NO API, WEBUI, LOG CLEAR, FAN CONTROL, PHYSICAL FAN, FAULT, WORKLOAD, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
